podcast-joerogan-Gd92fg1VWyU:
Rick Doblin shares a DMT story in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, a realization about Hitler that came to him during a trip. Doblin, the founder of MAPS, rarely hides the personal roots of his life's work. This short segment is one of his most retold tales.

He describes the experience and the thought it left him with about evil, guilt, and his own Jewish family's history. Rogan reacts and asks what Doblin did with the insight afterward. The segment shows the odd source of one man's mission: a drug experience that turned into a forty-year campaign for legal psychedelic therapy.
podcast-joerogan-QHfOR-byUyU:
Media theorist Douglas Rushkoff joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 346, from the show's early years. Rushkoff writes about how technology and media reshape people, and he was studying the digital age before it swallowed daily life. His visit has a time-capsule feel now.

He and Rogan talk about media, money, and the early web's promise and traps. Rushkoff argues that tools carry values, and users rarely notice them. The episode is worth hearing as a baseline: what a sharp media thinker feared and hoped before social feeds ran the world, recorded while that world was still forming.
podcast-tuckercarlson-nVWvqVu_FYU:
Donald Trump Jr. joins Tucker Carlson as threats against his father grow. The sample first notes a network film by James O'Keefe on cartel trafficking. Then the talk turns to family and safety.

Trump Jr. speaks as a son who has watched two attempts up close. He argues that harsh words from rivals fuel real danger. The title promises his plan to uproot political corruption. He links safety, justice, and reform into one pledge. The episode blends a son's worry with a campaign insider's vow to fight back. The worry in his voice never sounds staged.
